Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

Applicant is in judicial custody in FIR/Case Crime No. 17 of 2024, under Section 228A, 376, 452,
504, 506 Ipc, Section 67A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 and Section 3 (1) (w), 3 (2) (v)
of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Police Station
Transit Camp, District Udham Singh Nagar.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the FIR, the applicant and the informant both were working in a company for two years together from 2021 to 2023.
They came close to each other.

FIR records that in the month of February, 2023, one day, the applicant spiked the food of the informant and rape her on multiple occasion on that night and has also made gandi-gandi videos and thereafter, he continued blackmailing and establishing physical relations with the informant.
FIR also records that the applicant had made some videos viral on some social media platform.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant and the informant both are major; they were working together; their relationship was consensual; they both were living together as husband and wife; some dispute arose between them, due to which FIR has been lodged.
He would refer to the statement of Dileep Kumar, the landlord recorded during investigation.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that the informant has supported the prosecution case..
6. It is the stage of bail.
Much of the discussion is not expected of.
Arguments are being appreciated with the caveat that any observation made in this order shall have no bearing at any subsequent stage of the trial or in any other proceedings.

sentences.text: It is a case of long relationship between the parties.
Dileep Kumar, the landlord has stated that both the applicant and the informant were living as husband and wife.
8. Having considered the entirety of facts, this Court is of the view that the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.

9. The bail application is allowed.
10. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
(Ravindra Maithani, J) 13.08.2024 Jitendra Satyapal @ Guddu vs State Of Uttarakhand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173594290/
